language.script_notes: English dominant; French appears via federal bilingual signage but far less prominently than in Quebec.
false_friends: US Midwest (similarly flat farmland and grid roads)
Canadian Prairies' own vast uniformity making internal orientation hard

road_furniture.line_paint: As national; long, dead-straight rural section-line roads are extremely common given the flat terrain.
road_furniture.curb_style: Minimal outside towns; open roadside ditches in rural farmland.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national; grain elevator silhouettes on the horizon near small towns are a defining regional tell.

architecture.roof_style: Simple gable roofs on farmhouses; utilitarian small-town Main Street storefronts.
architecture.roof_material: Asphalt shingle and metal roofing widespread.
architecture.wall_construction: Wood-frame farmhouses; historic wooden, concrete or steel grain elevators standing beside rail lines in nearly every small town — the single strongest Prairie visual signature.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Weathered wood tones on grain elevators and farm buildings; simple painted storefronts in small towns.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Grain elevators (wooden, concrete or steel) beside rail lines in almost every town; simple prairie farmhouses; small-town Main Streets; oil/gas industry infrastructure in Alberta specifically.

nature.vegetation: Vast, flat cultivated cropland (wheat, canola, barley) stretching to the horizon; treeless or near-treeless in the driest southern stretches, transitioning to aspen parkland and boreal forest further north.
nature.terrain: Famously flat to gently rolling, part of the Great Plains — among the flattest, most open landscapes in Canada, with a huge sky-dominated horizon; the Rocky Mountains rise abruptly at the western edge of Alberta.
nature.climate_signature: Wide-open big-sky horizons over flat farmland; harsh snowy winters, hot summers — visually similar to the US Great Plains/Midwest but with Canadian road furniture and km/h signage.

vehicles.plate_color: Alberta red-on-white ('Wild Rose Country'), Saskatchewan and Manitoba each with their own distinct provincial designs (Manitoba dark blue on white).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Farm equipment (tractors, combines) visible in season; pickup trucks especially common given the region's agricultural and oil/gas economy.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of generations; dense modern coverage around Calgary/Edmonton/Winnipeg, older/thinner in remote rural areas.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good grid coverage of rural section-line roads similar to the US Midwest; some gaps in the most remote farmland.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Nearly identical flat farmland, grain elevators, grid road layout, similar climate
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Canadian speed signage is in km/h (vs. US mph); Canadian plates carry a province name and different colour schemes than US state plates; Canadian road furniture (bollard/guardrail styles) also differs from the US default.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Prairies are flat open farmland; the East is forested/lake-covered, the West is mountainous, and the North is Arctic tundra — all visually distinct.
